messages:
Anya: quick question after the all-hands: if an opportunistic pool in APAC loses capacity during peak, do we notify customers or try silent failover?
Marco: silent failover by default. runtime tries alternate pools and quantized-model cascade before surfacing an error. we will expose per-pool events in the infra status feed.
Ivy: can we get an example event payload so SEs know what customers will see?
Marco: example (pseudo):
```
event_type: pool_capacity_drop
pool: opportunistic-ap-east-1
severity: info
recommended_action: transparent_failover
````
deploy-bot: canary: autoscaler v1.7 -> opportunistic-ap-east-1 at 05:00 UTC.
Sam: leadership asked about communication windows for reserved pool migrations. what's the default notice?
Marco: 30 days notice and transfer credits for reserved capacity moves. customers on trials get longer notice.
Anya: last ask: alerts/SLAs 0, will SRE add a rapid alert for missed_tokens spikes?
Ivy: yes, proposed alert: missed_tokens/sec > 40 for 5m -> page on-call. Sam to review.
Sam: I'll formalize the alert and add it to the runbook. thanks all. closing thread.
